name: Stormwind Stockade
summary: Stormwind Stockade holds the city’s most dangerous prisoners beneath the canals near the Mage Quarter. A coordinated revolt has driven the guards from the lower cells, leaving the prison in chaos.

sections.title: A Prison Under Siege
sections.body: Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind keeps cutthroats, Defias operatives, captured Blackrock orcs, and Dark Iron dwarves. Now a violent uprising led by the Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd has forced the guards from the lower cells. The prisoners roam freely through the corridors. Thelwater has managed to secure the entrance, but the revolt still threatens to reach the canals. He depends on adventurers to enter the prison and put down the uprising.

sections.title: Bureaucracy and Backroom Schemes
sections.body: The House of Nobles has used the Stockade to hold prisoners whose fates serve its political aims. Murderers and other high-value prisoners sentenced to death elsewhere have had their executions delayed by aristocratic interference. Among them are Dextren Ward, a graverobber from Duskwood, and Targorr the Dread, a Blackrock executioner from Redridge. Ironforge has also taken notice. When human bureaucracy delays justice, it secretly hires mercenaries to execute dangerous prisoners such as Kam Deepfury.

faq.q: Where is the entrance to the Stockade located?
faq.answer: The entrance is in Stormwind City's canal district, on the northern bend beside the bridge into the Mage Quarter. A guarded doorway leads down a stone stairwell to the underground cells.

faq.q: Who started the riot inside the prison?
faq.answer: Bazil Thredd planned and began the revolt. The imprisoned Defias Brotherhood ringleader led the prisoners in overpowering the guards, taking their weapons, and seizing the underground cellblocks.

faq.q: Why are there orcs and Dark Iron dwarves in a Stormwind jail?
aliases: why are there orcs in stockades
faq.answer: Stormwind holds hostile prisoners captured across its contested territories. Targorr the Dread was taken from the Redridge Mountains, while Kam Deepfury represents the Dark Iron threat. Some are kept as military prisoners; others remain alive by noble decree, held for political leverage instead of being executed swiftly.

faq.q: Why are Duskwood and Redridge asking people to kill prisoners here?
faq.answer: Darkshire and Lakeshire sentenced Dextren Ward and Targorr the Dread to death, but the House of Nobles stayed their executions. Frustrated by Stormwind's interference, local leaders quietly hire sellswords to carry out the sentences.

angles.text: As an Alliance hero, you can see why keeping the Stockade secure matters to Stormwind's defense. Its halls reveal how far the Defias Brotherhood has reached into the capital.
As a rogue, you can read the riot as a glimpse of the Defias Brotherhood's operations under Bazil Thredd. The criminal underworld is deeply organized beneath the crown's nose.
